sources.label: World Bank WDI, fertility rate (births per woman)
Taub Center, Why are there so many children in Israel?

lines.line: Since nineteen ninety, only one of these lines went up.
Babies per woman, traded like a stock.
Europe first. In nineteen sixty, about two and a half.
Spain, one point one. Italy, one point two. Germany, one point four.
Israel? Down from almost four, then flat near three.
Middle East: Saudi Arabia, Iran, Syria and Jordan started above seven.
The Emirates, one point two. Turkey, one and a half. Iran, one point seven.
Even Egypt and Jordan are now below Israel.
Since nineteen ninety: sixteen red arrows, one green.
Why? The Taub Center finds a strong family culture at every level of religion.
Even secular and traditional Israelis average over two kids.
A rich, modern country, still investing in the future.
So, which line would you buy?

transcript.heard: Since 1990, only one of these lines went up. Babies per woman, traded like a stock. Europe first. In 1960, about 2.5. Spain, 1.1. Italy, 1.2. Germany, 1.4. Israel? Down from almost 4, then flat near 3. Middle East. Saudi Arabia, Iran, Syria, and Jordan started above 7. The Emirates, 1.2. Turkey, 1.5. Iran, 1.7. Even Egypt and Jordan are now below Israel. Since 1990, 16 red arrows, one green. Israel, up almost 2%. Why? The top center finds a strong family culture at every level of religion. Even secular and traditional Israelis average over two kids. A rich, modern country, still investing in the future. So, which line would you buy?
